pages:
I found this book far from the ruins of Valdren.

Unlike the records of Ashenreach and Eldoria, this one was not written by a king or an elder.

It belonged to someone who worked in the shadows.

A spy.

The book was hidden beneath the floor of a ruined house.

I almost missed it.

Most of the pages contain names, dates, locations, and information about the other kingdoms.

But the final pages are different.

They were written in a hurry.

Whatever happened to this person...

they knew they were running out of time.

THE SPY'S RECORD

Valdren has never been the strongest kingdom.

We do not have Ashenreach's armies.

We do not have Eldoria's scholars.

We do not have Myrath's warriors.

So we learned to survive differently.

We listen.

We watch.

We collect.

Information is our greatest weapon.

Our people travel between kingdoms, taking whatever work allows us to get close enough to listen.

Merchants.

Guards.

Travellers.

Sometimes even soldiers.

We hear things that kings would never say in front of their people.

We see things that armies never notice.

And when we return...

we bring everything home.

Ashenreach pays for military information.

Eldoria pays for discoveries.

Myrath pays for information about enemy movements.

Everyone wants to know something.

And Valdren knows how to find it.

For years, this was how we survived.
Until we started looking into Eldoria.

At first, it was simple.

We wanted information.

We wanted to know what their scholars were studying.

What they had discovered.

Why they had suddenly become so secretive.

Then our people started disappearing.

The first spy never returned.

We assumed he had been caught.

The second returned.

But he was not the same.

He could barely speak.

He kept asking us the same question.
"Did you see it?"

We did not know what he meant.

We asked him what he had seen.

He would not tell us.

He only kept talking about Eldoria.

He said the scholars had found something.

Something far more dangerous than anything we had ever reported.

He said it was beneath the ruins.

He said they had opened something.

Then he stopped speaking.

Three days later...

he disappeared.

His room was locked from the inside.

There was nothing wrong with the door.

Nothing broken.

Nothing stolen.

He was simply gone.

Eldoria has gone silent.

No messages.

No merchants.

No scholars.

Nothing.

We sent another spy.

He returned after six days.

He was terrified.

He said the city was empty.

Not destroyed.

Empty.

The laboratories were still intact.

Books were lying open.

Experiments were still running.

Meals had been left on tables.

But there was nobody there.

He said he found the council chamber.

There were twelve chairs.

Eleven were empty.

The twelfth had blood on it.

He refused to tell us whose.

Then he said something strange.

He said there was writing on the wall.
Three words.
IT KNOWS.

I asked him what it meant.

He looked at me.

Then he asked:
"Did you see it?"

I told him no.

He said:

"Good."

We have sent no one else.

Whatever happened to Eldoria is still there.

I know this because our people have started seeing things near the border.

Figures in places where nobody should be.

Lights beneath the ground.

Voices coming from abandoned buildings.

Sometimes footsteps.

Sometimes whispers.

Always at night.

And every time someone investigates...

nothing is there.

I have spent my entire life collecting secrets.

I have never been afraid of them.

But this is different.

This is something we cannot watch.

Something we cannot understand.

Something we cannot sell.

For the first time...

Valdren has information that nobody wants to hear.

We found another record.

It was older than Eldoria.

Older than Ashenreach.

Older than any kingdom.

The symbols on it are the same symbols we found beneath the ruins.

I have seen them before.

So has our council.

We were told never to speak of them.

I asked why.

Nobody answered.

I asked again.

Still nothing.

Then the oldest member of the council told me something.

He said:
"Some things are better left forgotten."

I asked him how he knew.

He told me his grandfather had said the same thing.

And his grandfather had learned it from someone else.

The warning has been passed down for generations.
But nobody remembers who started it.

Tonight I found something in my room.

I do not know how it got there.

A piece of stone.

The same kind found beneath Eldoria.

There is a symbol carved into it.

I have never seen this symbol before.

But I recognize it.

I saw it in the old records.

I thought the records were wrong.
They were not.

There is another name written beneath it.

I cannot read the language.

But I have copied it here.
Perhaps someone in Myrath will know.

We believe Ashenreach is responsible.

They were the first to search for powers they did not understand.

They were the first to become obsessed with them.

And now Eldoria is gone.

We cannot wait for the same thing to happen to us.

We need warriors.

We need someone who can fight.

So we are going to Myrath.

We will tell them everything.

Every secret.

Every report.

Every piece of information we have gathered.

Maybe they will believe us.

Maybe they won't.

But we have no other choice.

If what we saw in Eldoria is only the beginning...

then this is no longer about Valdren.

Or Eldoria.

Or Ashenreach.
Something far more dangerous is coming.

And this time...

there may be nowhere left to hide.

MY NOTES

The final pages were written by someone else.

The handwriting is different.

Older.

The spy's record ends before they ever reach Myrath.

I found no evidence that the journey was completed.

But there is something strange.

The stone mentioned in the record was still inside the book.

I compared its markings with the symbols I found beneath Ashenreach and Eldoria.

They match.

Exactly.

There is one more thing.

The name beneath the symbol...

I have seen it before.

Not in a book.

Not on a ruin.
It was carved into a wall near the arena.

I did not notice it at first.

Someone had tried to remove it.

They had scratched over the letters until the stone was almost destroyed.

But the name is still there.

I copied it before leaving.

I do not know what it means.

I only know one thing.

Valdren believed Ashenreach caused everything.

Eldoria believed they had discovered something ancient.

And the spy believed something was coming.

Perhaps all three were wrong.

Or perhaps...

they were all looking at different pieces of the same thing.
There is only one kingdom left whose records I have not found.
Myrath.

If the final records exist...

they may contain the answer.
Or they may tell me why there is no answer left to find.
